labels.expectedValue: Modified gross with a calendar-year-2006 Base Year stop — Tenant pays Additional Rent equal to the excess of annual Operating Costs per rentable square foot over the Base Year amount, with controllable Operating Costs capped at a 6% year-over-year increase (Uncontrollable Expenses — utilities, insurance, real estate taxes, and similar — are excluded from that cap). Taxes and Insurance are separately passed through above their own Base Year amounts, with a gross-up provision.

labels.expectedValue: Yes, in two circumstances: (1) Condemnation — the Lease terminates automatically on a full Taking of the Building/Premises; Tenant may terminate on a partial Taking that denies use of the Premises for 180+ days, cuts remaining parking below 80% of its prior level, or eliminates all access; Landlord may terminate on a material partial Taking, conditioned on also terminating every other terminable lease in the Building. (2) Casualty — Tenant may terminate if Landlord estimates repairs will exceed 180 days, or if repair proceeds prove inadequate and Landlord won't fund the shortfall; Landlord may terminate if repairs are estimated to exceed 180 days, damage exceeds 50% of replacement cost during the Lease's final year, restoration would cost $500,000+ and is uneconomical, or a mortgagee requires the insurance proceeds (also conditioned on terminating every other terminable lease in the Building).
labels.notes: p.20, Section 14 (Condemnation); p.21-22, Section 15 (Fire or Other Casualty)
